https://www.thetablet.co.uk/news/polish-.text: Polish bishops condemn education changes ahead of new school year Adam Easton 24 August 2026, The Tablet Prev Next The Polish Episcopal Conference previously backed legal challenges to the cuts to religious education classes. Daniel Ibañez / EWTN News At the start of the 2025-2026 academic year, the Ministry of Education cut religious education classes in schools from two hours per week to one, and required that those classes be scheduled directly before or after compulsory classes. Poland’s bishops called for the restoration of religious education in schools ahead of the start of the new academic year. In a statement on 24 August titled “Young People Deserve More”, the Polish Episcopal Conference (KEP) said religious education classes should return to their proper place in school timetables and criticised the government’s decision to make health education classes mandatory from September. “At the threshold of a new school year and in the face of the serious challenges facing education, the Presidium of the Polish Episcopal Conference feels obliged to speak out in the spirit of pastoral care for the young generations in our homeland,” it said. At the start of the 2025-2026 academic year, the Ministry of Education cut religious education classes in schools from two hours per week to one, and required that those classes be scheduled directly before or after compulsory classes. The classes essentially teach the Catholic catechism and rarely include information on other religions. Grades from religious education classes no longer count towards a pupil’s average grade each year. “We appeal for the immediate restoration of these classes to their proper place and for a genuine dialogue with religious communities,” the KEP statement said. It backed a citizen’s bill sent to parliament that proposes the restoration of a weekly two hours of religious education or ethics classes with results counting towards final grades. The bishops also expressed concern about the ministry’s decision to make health education classes compulsory at the start of this academic year. The classes were introduced last year but attendance was optional and only around 30 per cent of pupils nationwide chose to attend. The ministry said pupils will still be able to opt out of the classes this year when they deal with matters concerning sexual health. The KEP said it recognises the need for health education in schools and its important role in the promotion of mental health and in disease prevention. “Our concerns, however, are about the vision of humanity, marriage and family that emerge from the curriculum and published textbooks,” the statement said. “Education in such a sensitive area of human life must respect the parents’ right to decide on its shape. The state should support the family in its upbringing, not take over its basic functions,” it continued. “Sexuality should be presented in the context of marital and family relationships because in this context it serves the true good of humanity. The lack of a clear position that marriage is a union between a man and a woman is also concerning.” Polish bishops ask for new talks with government to find education deal Poland’s election – learning to live with the secular state Stay updated — add us as a preferred news source on Google: CATHOLIC NEWS Church-state relations Education Poland Polish bishops’ conference Polish Catholics sex education The Catholic Church in Poland Help us keep The Tablet’s voice independent, clear and far-reaching. https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liv.text: Flights at Liverpool John Lennon Airport and across the UK have faced major disruption today due to air traffic control problems. Airpace in northern and central England, as well as in Scotland and Northern Ireland was struck by the issue at the National Air Traffic Services (NATS). NATS confirmed that the issue was fixed shortly after 10.30am today, September 21. A NATS spokesperson said: "The issue in our Prestwick centre is now fixed. We are working with airports and airlines to safely lift air traffic regulations as quickly as we can to minimise any further disruption. "Passengers should still check the status of their flight with their airline. We apologise for the disruption." NATS has said that the issue is unrelated to problems earlier this month when around 2,000 flights were cancelled due to a NATS software defect. After the issue was fixed, Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said on social media: “There has been a further IT issue affecting Nats. Engineers have fixed the problem and systems are resuming. “I know this will be deeply frustrating for passengers after the previous issue. There may be some delays as things reset. Please check with your airline for updates.” A number of flights departing from and arriving at Liverpool John Lennon Airport are facing delays, with some incoming flights being cancelled altogether. The 1.05pm easyJet flight from Derry, the 2.40pm easyJet flight from Prague, and 3.45pm easyJet flight from Nice have all been cancelled, with passengers being instructed to contact their airline. A number of other arrivals are expected to be delayed, with the 1.05pm from Sofia now expected at 1.30pm, the 1.15pm from Krakow expected at 3.05pm, and the 2.55pm from Dublin expected at 3.55pm. The 3.45pm RyanAir flight from Liverpool to Dublin has been delayed by one hour, and the 4.45pm Jet2 flight to Dalaman has been put back to 5.15pm. On X, a Liverpool John Lennon Airport spokesperson said: "The earlier technical issue experienced by NATS causing air traffic control problems has now been fixed with operations starting to return to normal, however some flights are subject to delay due to the knock on effects of the earlier disruption. Passengers are advised to contact their airline for the latest information regarding particular flights." Manchester Airport was also hit by the widespread disruption. In a statement a spokesperson said: "NATS has reported that the issue affecting one of its air traffic control sites in Scotland has been fixed. "Operations are returning to normal but some flights may still be affected by delays as a result of the earlier problem. Passengers due to travel today are advised to check for updates from their airline” 1.05pm easyJet flight from Derry, Northern Ireland 2.40pm easyJet flight from Prague, Czech Republic 3.45pm easyJet flight from Nice, France 11.15am easyJet flight U22113 to Paris is cancelled 12.55pm easyJet flight U2711 to Newquay is cancelled 8.30pm Ryanair flight FR3238 to Brussels is cancelled
